This expanded, enhanced second edition of the best-selling game features all-new illustrations by artists Josh Emrich and Lisk Feng, offers new gameplay elements from designer Henry Audubon, and incorporates the most interesting ideas from each of the Parks games and expansions: the additional camping module from Parks: Nightfall, the animal integrations from Parks: Wildlife, and a comprehensive selection of players’ favorite gear, challenges, and mechanics from the five-year history of Parks (along with some new surprises). Over the course of three rounds (called Seasons), your two hikers will make their way along the path, stopping at trail sites, collecting resources to visit parks, taking photos of beautiful vistas, and encountering wildlife. Along the way, you’ll get gear to upgrade your experience, spend a night at a campsite, fill your canteen for special bonuses, and indulge your unique passion for the outdoors. At the end of the third Season, the hike (and the game) is over! Count up your points and see who had the greatest experience in Acadia, Grand Teton, Mount Rainier, Crater Lake, Everglades, Denali, Canyonlands, and all the rest of our national parks. [Rating: 1/10] Poorly play tested, only one avenue for gathering the most victory points. Side mechanics to gain victory points will put player significantly behind rather than just visiting parks. Avoid this game, don't let the aesthetic fool you, it's a 1 dimensional game.

[Rating: 1/10] Beautiful card art and I love the theme but that is about it.  I did not like Tokaido but that is way better than this. – No decisions.  Collect resources to convert into points.   – No tension, finishing early does nothing – Random start goal is not important (maybe 10% of points just buy the highest value parks) – Random bonus for seasons, random parks turning up – Long I was ready to finish after 2/3 seasons

[Rating: 1/10] Zen game I thought it was a tourist attraction game but after watching playthrough, it is a camera game Interesting game mechanic: Evolving map Useful components: Park cards can be easily used as monopoly/exploration tiles

[Rating: 1/10] Boring and fairly mindless but otherwise inoffensive family weight set collection game, nothing particularly wrong with it but at the same time nothing about it stands out as interesting to make it worthwhile playing it over any other option.

[Rating: 1.9/10] Mechanically really poor.... mediocre game which is sad.  The design is not enough.

[Rating: 2/10] 1 Play Absolutely spectacular artwork. Gameplay itself is straight-forward and still has enough depth to be a decent filler. Not a lot in it that I particularly enjoy though from a game-play standpoint. Would not mind playing this once in a really long while.  On a side-note, I am still not a fan of this sort of worker placement kind of interaction in games at all. The interaction really feels forced rather than an outcome of actual decisions made by a player to hinder another player or to further his own prospects at the cost of others.
